narrative:
The model determined that you have a 26% chance of representing a bad credit risk. While this is not an extremely high probability, it was enough for the bank to deny your loan application.

The three factors that most strongly influenced this decision were your savings account status, the status of your checking account, and your other installment plans. 

Your lack of any savings or unknown savings pushed the prediction most strongly toward bad credit risk. Among approved applicants, only 33% have no savings or unknown savings, while nearly half have less than 100 DM. This absence of visible reserves signaled higher risk to the model. 

Your checking account, which shows no balance, was the second most important factor and also increased the likelihood of being seen as a bad credit risk. In contrast, 59% of approved applicants have no checking account balance, but the model still weighed your specific combination unfavorably.

The fact that you have other installment plans through a bank was the third most influential feature. This actually worked in your favor and pushed the prediction toward good credit, yet it was not enough to overcome the concerns raised by your savings and checking situation.

Your requested loan duration of 48 months, more than double the average of approved loans, and the higher installment rate relative to your income likely compounded these issues.

To improve your chances on a future application, focus on building verifiable savings, maintaining a positive checking account balance, and reducing other installment obligations before reapplying. Consider requesting a shorter loan term as well.
